slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing and transferring contact-rich human bathing demonstrations to a soft robotic hand, contributing to the development of safe physical human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing, reconstructing, and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a soft-robotic hand.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as a processing primitive to synchronize motion, shape, and force data, enabling retargeting of clinician demonstrations to a tendon-driven soft hand.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world deployment on a mannequin using open- and closed-loop control.
card.limitation: Significant sim-to-real gap; closed-loop control uses aggregate pressure sums rather than distributions; not yet ready for human subjects.

slides.title: AdaDexGrasp: Adaptive Dexterous Grasping via 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Fusion
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE DEXTEROUS GRASPING VIA VISUO-TACTILE FUSION
slides.highlight: This framework integrates 3D visual perception with tactile feedback to enable contact-aware grasp generation and dynamic refinement, improving success rates across diverse objects.

card.one_liner: AdaDexGrasp improves dexterous grasping by fusing 3D object geometry with finger-identity-aware tactile feedback for adaptive refinement.
card.key_idea: A unified framework using a semantic contact map for initial pose generation, a stability classifier, and a diffusion-based adaptation model to iteratively refine grasps via visuo-tactile point clouds.
card.evaluation: Tested on 50 objects in IsaacGym and 20+ real-world objects; outperformed 10 baselines, achieving 83% success on unseen categories in simulation.
card.limitation: Denser tactile modalities (e.g., shear forces) were avoided due to higher data requirements and increased sim-to-real gaps.

slides.title: Detection and Ranging of Transient Extrinsic Contacts Based on 6D Dynamic Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: FAST EXTRINSIC CONTACT DETECTION AND RANGING
slides.highlight: This work introduces TECDAR for rapid, millimeter-level localization of extrinsic contacts, supporting the physics-based skill estimation and delicate manipulation goals of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: TECDAR enables fast, millimeter-level extrinsic contact localization on grasped objects using a single 6D IMU sensor.
card.key_idea: An event-driven framework using an accelerometer for contact triggering and an Extended Kalman Filter to map gyroscopic angular velocity and robot pose to contact coordinates.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on line and point-contact tasks (e.g., books, pens) achieving ~7mm average accuracy and 20ms control response cycles.
card.limitation: Higher localization error (5.36mm) compared to high-resolution visuotactile sensors like GelSlim 3.0.

slides.title: VIDP: Variable Impedance Diffusion Policy for Compliant Robot Manipulation from Diverse Demonstrations
slides.tldr: LEARNING VARIABLE IMPEDANCE CONTROL FROM KINEMATIC DATA
slides.highlight: This framework enables robots to predict pose actions and task compliance from diverse demonstrations without requiring force sensors.

card.one_liner: VIDP learns variable impedance control from kinematic demonstrations to enable compliant, contact-rich robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: A Task-Parameterized Directionality-Aware Mixture Model (TP-DAMM) extracts stiffness profiles from trajectory variances, which a Diffusion Policy then uses to jointly predict pose and compliance.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Peg-in-Hole, Pulley Assembly, and Cable Routing tasks. VIDP outperformed fixed-impedance baselines in success rates and reduced interaction forces.
card.limitation: The provided text does not clearly state a specific limitation or risk when using the framework.

slides.title: Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision for Reliable Dual-Arm Surgical Subtask Manipulation
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE EXECUTION HORIZON FOR SURGICAL VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a test-time mechanism to improve the reliability of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in surgical robotics by adaptively truncating action sequences based on trajectory divergence.

card.one_liner: TDHD improves surgical VLA reliability by adaptively truncating open-loop action sequences based on trajectory divergence.
card.key_idea: A test-time mechanism measuring L2 distance between two flow-matching trajectories generated with small noise perturbations to trigger replanning via absolute and ratio thresholds.
card.evaluation: Tested on a da Vinci-like dual-arm robot using 600 teleoperated demonstrations; success rates rose to 60% (needle) and 80% (tissue) over VLA baselines.
card.limitation: Evaluations were limited to controlled phantom environments and a small set of subtasks, lacking diverse anatomies and longer procedures.

slides.title: Embodied Multimodal Grounding for Open-Vocabulary Mobile Manipulation via Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting
slides.tldr: EMBODIED MULTIMODAL GROUNDING FOR MOBILE MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal grounding framework using Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting to improve robustness under clutter and occlusion, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and scene reasoning.

card.one_liner: A multimodal grounding framework using Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting to improve open-vocabulary mobile manipulation robustness.
card.key_idea: Integrates active multi-view Semantic-3DGS for 3D localization and obstacle reasoning, reachability-aware base positioning, and late-block semantic injection into a diffusion-based VLA policy.
card.evaluation: Real-robot tests (50 trials) against PointVLA and DexVLA; achieved 60% long-horizon and 74% cluttered success rates using a Unitree Go2 platform.
card.limitation: Targets quasi-static manipulation; requires off-board GPU and cannot perform fast dynamic interactions or zero-shot skill acquisition.

slides.title: TCAM for Autonomous Deformable Manipulation
slides.highlight: A champion system for deformable manipulation uses the TCAM framework and a multi-view VLA backbone to autonomously pick, align, and smooth T-shirts.

card.one_liner: A champion autonomous system for T-shirt picking and smoothing using a causal action learning framework.
card.key_idea: TCAM integrates a custom 3D-printed gripper, four-view wrist perception, and a closed-loop VLA policy refined through iterative causal failure analysis and targeted data recollection.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in WBCD 2026 Track 4; loaded 25 T-shirts (22 smooth) at ~23s per attempt, securing first place.
card.limitation: Lacks an autonomous failure detector; early-termination decisions during competition were made by human supervisors.

slides.title: C2Dex: Contact-Consistent Reconstruction and Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Monocular Video
slides.highlight: C2Dex improves the transfer of human manipulation behaviors from monocular video to robots by using stable object-side contacts to ensure physically plausible interactions and geometry preservation.

card.one_liner: C2Dex converts monocular human videos into executable dexterous robot trajectories using stable object-side contact representations.
card.key_idea: Aggregates frame-wise observations into stable canonical object-space contacts, using them as constraints for HOI reconstruction and targets for Laplacian interaction-preserving retargeting and residual RL refinement.
card.evaluation: Tested on DexYCB and TACO datasets; achieved success rates of 57.78% and 26.67%, significantly outperforming baselines. Validated via real-robot replay on Unitree G1.
card.limitation: Struggles with severe occlusions, extreme viewpoints, object pose drift, and complex in-hand manipulations like finger gaiting.
